title: t-SNE & UMAP for Visualization
interviewAnswer: t-SNE and UMAP create low-dimensional embeddings that emphasize neighborhood structure, mainly for exploration/visualization. Global distances and cluster sizes can be misleading, especially with t-SNE.
keyPoints: Do not treat 2D distance as ground truth.
Use PCA or task metrics alongside visualization.
why: t-SNE & UMAP for Visualization appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
intuition: Do not treat 2D distance as ground truth.
deepDive: t-SNE and UMAP create low-dimensional embeddings that emphasize neighborhood structure, mainly for exploration/visualization. Global distances and cluster sizes can be misleading, especially with t-SNE. Hyperparameters change plots. Use PCA or task metrics alongside visualization. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Visualize embedding neighborhoods to inspect class overlap, but evaluate retrieval quantitatively rather than trusting clusters on the plot.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does t-SNE & UMAP for Visualization make?
How would you validate or debug t-SNE & UMAP for Visualization in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.

visual.title: Embedding visualization
visual.caption: t-SNE and UMAP are useful for exploring local structure, but distances and apparent cluster separation can be misleading.
